chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) regarding

a man who swears in dissimulation (taqiyyah). He (peace be upon him) said: If you fear for your wealth and your life, then swear to repel it with your oath. But if you see that this does not repel anything, then do not swear for them.

key_terms.تَقِيَّة: Dissimulation; concealing one's true beliefs or status to avoid harm in times of danger or oppression.
key_terms.دَم: Blood; referring to one's life or physical safety.
key_terms.يَمِين: Oath; a solemn declaration invoking God's name.

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to swear an oath for taqiyyah to protect wealth or life?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the pragmatic application of taqiyyah, emphasizing that the permissibility of an oath is contingent upon its efficacy in averting harm rather than being an absolute obligation. It reflects the Shia scholarly principle of 'maslaha' (public interest), where the oath serves as a protective tool only when it successfully repels the immediate threat to one's wealth or life. This nuanced ruling distinguishes between mere verbal dissimulation and effective strategic concealment.
